weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory, snow accumulations up to 6
inches. For the Winter Storm Watch Above 5, 000 feet, heavy snow
possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 2 feet expected
above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet above 8,000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For
the Winter Storm Watch, from late Tuesday night through late
Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

weather.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 15 at 7:32PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory, snow accumulations up to 6
inches. For the Winter Storm Watch Above 5, 000 feet, heavy snow
possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 2 feet expected
above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet above 8,000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For
the Winter Storm Watch, from late Tuesday night through late
Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 PM CST this
evening through late Thursday night. For the High Surf
Advisory, from 2 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and

swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 1:28AM EST until November 19 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to
1 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:53 AM Wednesday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 8:51AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 2
feet expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet
above 8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...Until Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM CST Tuesday the stage was 15.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late tonight and continue falling to 11.0 feet by Sunday morning. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: McMullen, TX

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:27AM CST until November 18 at 7:36PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Tuesday the stage was 15.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tonight and continue falling to 11.0 feet by Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
weather.areaDesc: McMullen, TX

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected in the Eastern Sierra. For elevations between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 10 to 18 inches expected. For elevations between 8,000 and 9,500 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 18 to 36 inches expected. Locally higher totals expected above 9,500 feet. Winds could gust as high as 55 mph. * WHERE...Eastern Sierra Slopes. * WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and power lines. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Whiteout conditions are expected and will make travel treacherous and potentially life-threatening.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 1:44PM CST until November 19 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, until 6 AM CST
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1105 PM tonight and again at 1049 PM Thursday night.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San Pablo Bay. * WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 2:01AM CST until November 19 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or
pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except
those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable
to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of
Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

location.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River; Lower Matanuska Valley; NW Kenai Peninsula; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie, and Martin counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal counties. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on snow is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam Gulch. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways. Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This includes the city of Seward. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday. Southerly to southeasterly winds will shift to more easterly early Thursday morning, limiting precipitation amounts in lee of the mountains for areas along the Seward Highway from roughly Moose Pass and southward to Seward. Rainfall is on track to decrease late Thursday afternoon. Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and ponding of water on roadways. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:

promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

The hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday morning and evening commutes. Visibilities may drop below 1/4 mile due to falling and blowing snow.

location.region: Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 11:52AM PST until November 20 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Elko NV
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in Elko County.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 4 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday morning and evening
commutes. Visibilities may drop below 1/4 mile due to falling and
blowing snow.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at 1049 PM tonight, 1104 AM Thursday, and 1041 Thursday night.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: At 130 pm, widespread showers are ongoing across the Middle to Upper Florida Keys and surrounding near and offshore waters within a mesoscale convective complex. This activity is producing pockets of wind gusts of 20 to 25 knots and reduced visibility from moderate to heavy downpours. Activity is slowly propagating eastward and circulating around a small scale area of low pressure currently centered in the Straits of Florida approximately 30 nautical miles south of Marathon. Showers are diminishing from west to east, and rain has ended in the waters near Key West through Big Pine Key. Strong easterly wind gusts are occurring along the western periphery of the decaying precipitation in the waters south of the Middle Keys. These higher winds may only last for an hour or two before decreasing.

In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday night. For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight CST Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 12:11PM CST until November 22 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7
feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight CST Thursday
night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Weather Service when you can do so safely.

events.title: High Wind Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Southwest winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts up to 80 mph. * WHERE...Pribilof Islands. * WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and cause power outages. Travel will be difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds are currently peaking this morning and will stay elevated through the rest of the morning and into the early afternoon. Strong winds will diminish through the rest of this afternoon into the evening hours. As a result of the long duration of westerly winds, wave heights of 25 to 30 ft within 15 to 20 nautical miles of Saint Paul are expected through this afternoon. Ongoing precipitation has been observed as snow. In conjunction with strong winds, visibility may drop to as low as one mile at times in stronger snow showers this morning.

events.description: AVAREV The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S. Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center. BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED 08:55 PST Wed Nov 18 2026 The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA)) * WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger is anticipated in the backcountry from around sunset on Wednesday into early Friday morning. * WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass(Hwy 4) on the south, including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs exist. * WHEN...In effect from Wed 08:55 PST to Thu 05:00 PST. * IMPACTS...Significant snowfall may lead to widespread avalanche activity in the mountains. Large avalanches capable of burying or injuring people could occur in backcountry areas. * PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche conditions could occur in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain during HIGH avalanche danger is not recommended. Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org for more detailed information. Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday morning. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Flash Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall continue to be possible over the Pickett burn area. * WHERE...Areas northeast of Calistoga in Napa County. * WHEN...Through this evening. * IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Pickett burn area is expected during the period of the watch. Residents near the Pickett burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the Simmons Canyon and areas near and between Pickett Road to Silverado Trail. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead to flash flooding and debris flows. - Some locations that may experience flash flooding include... Areas northeast of Calistoga. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

and television for statements and possible warnings. Follow the
advice of public safety officials.
